newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in Dec - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in Dec - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.8 percent in the first week of fiscal December versus November, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 6.0 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 6.0 percent in the week ended December 7 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research, said sales for the week were slightly below plan.

"I wouldn't be too concerned about that," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "We're just a shade below where we thought (sales) would be and where stores thought they would be."
So far in December, chain stores have led discount and department stores, Eilenberg said.
Apparel, accessories and women's outerwear sold particularly well in the survey period, he said.
Holiday sales seem to be on track, Eilenberg said. "We think the stores will come in as expected for the two months."
